# Practice Jazz Chords

> Free jazz chord flashcards in the browser: the app shows one bar of chords at a time, in tempo, in all 12 keys, to practice jazz chords and progressions in every key.

Practice Jazz Chords (https://practice-jazz-chords.com/) is a practice tool for jazz musicians on any instrument. It needs no account and no installation; settings are stored in the browser.

- Exercises: Major 7, Minor 7, Dominant 7, a random mix of the three, ii7–V7–Imaj7, ii7(b5)–V7–Im6 and Imaj7–vi7–ii7–V7 (each progression in one bar or spread over two bars), and custom progressions written in Roman numerals.
- Key order: Random, Weighted Cycle, Perfect 4th up and Perfect 4th down.
- Key ratings (1–5 stars per key) make unfamiliar keys come up more often; this can be turned off.
- A one-bar count-in, a click on every beat, an optional bass root note, tempo from 20 to 300 BPM and keyboard shortcuts.
- Installable as an app (PWA) that also works offline.

## Docs

- [Documentation](https://practice-jazz-chords.com/documentation/): how every part of the app works
- [Getting started](https://practice-jazz-chords.com/documentation/#getting-started): a practice session in four steps
- [Custom progressions](https://practice-jazz-chords.com/documentation/#custom): syntax for writing your own progressions in Roman numerals, with examples
- [Key order](https://practice-jazz-chords.com/documentation/#key-order): how the next key is chosen
- [Key ratings](https://practice-jazz-chords.com/documentation/#key-ratings): how ratings change how often a key comes up
- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://practice-jazz-chords.com/documentation/#shortcuts)
- [Full documentation as Markdown](https://practice-jazz-chords.com/llms-full.txt)
